change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.18.0 (package-lock.json), which is far behind the new 1.0.0 major. Nothing breaks today: older SDKs keep sending anthropic-version 2023-06-01. The upgrade is optional, but it is the single move that brings the repo onto API version 2026-10-21. The one call site (server.js:49) uses only model, max_tokens and messages, none of the removed sampling params. Uncertainties for the migration agent: response handling was not read, so check how the response content is consumed after the jump across many SDK minors. Also confirm messages carry no document blocks or citations, and check for any global OpenTelemetry tracer provider. The model claude-3-haiku-20240307 is not retired by any change in this batch, but it is very old; verify it is still available when testing the upgrade.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. The repo only moves from anthropic-version 2023-06-01 to 2026-10-21 by upgrading @anthropic-ai/sdk to 1.0.0, which sends the new version by default. The API-version move is the same edit as this SDK bump.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). OpenTelemetry spans are created automatically from SDK 0.134.0 onward. The repo is on 0.18.0, so this only applies once it upgrades past 0.134. The migration agent should check whether server.js registers a global tracer provider and, if so, decide whether to pass openTelemetry:false.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: messages.create runs through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.18.0, which is in the affected range <1.0.0. Upgrading to 1.0.0 switches this call to API version 2026-10-21. The call sends only model, max_tokens and messages, so the removed temperature/top_p/top_k parameters are not used. server.js is plain JS, so the MessageParam union change has no type impact.

record.prBody:
## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.18.0 -> 1.0.0 via npm (lockfile rewritten). server.js now joins text blocks of response.content instead of content[0].text (ContentBlock is a union). Added test/sdk.test.js (mocked fetch) asserting anthropic-version 2026-10-21, no temperature/top_p/top_k, SDK 1.x. No global OpenTelemetry tracer provider is registered, so no openTelemetry:false needed. No Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry usage, no document/citation blocks.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `server.js`
- `test/sdk.test.js`

### Why

SDK 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default and makes ContentBlock/MessageParam unions; the single messages.create call needed its response handling narrowed.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| sdk-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- sdk-test, added by the agent: `node test/sdk.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Before the baseline the harness ran `cd client && npm install --ignore-scripts` (The root postinstall (cd client && npm install) did not run, so client dependencies such as react-scripts are missing. The build runs in client via `npm run build`.); it exited 0.
- Preparation changed repo files, kept out of this PR: client/package-lock.json.

Test of this change: `sdk-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real API behaviour at 2026-10-21 not tested live
- claude-3-haiku-20240307 availability not verified
- Any new npm audit warnings / Apache-2.0 license change of the SDK not reviewed
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Bot reply is now all text blocks joined, rather than only the first block's text
- Requests now send anthropic-version 2026-10-21 instead of 2023-06-01

---

review.summary: The one named call site (server.js:49) already avoids the removed sampling params (no temperature/top_p/top_k), and it does not need Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry. The package bump is consistent across package.json and the lockfile, and the new test confirms the SDK sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21. The checks do not touch the real app path, though. The new test builds its own client against a mocked fetch, so server.js's rewritten response handling is never exercised. No live call proves that model `claude-3-haiku-20240307` is still accepted under API version 2026-10-21. Other scripts in the repo that may use the SDK were not reviewed. 'verified' is defensible for the SDK bump itself, but not for end-to-end behaviour.

concerns.issue: Line ~57: `response.content[0].text` became a map/join over text blocks. This goes beyond what the migration forces. Multiple text blocks are now concatenated, and an empty or non-text `content` now returns HTTP 200 with an empty `response` string instead of throwing and returning 500. The client may show a blank bubble where it used to show an error. No check covers this line, because test/sdk.test.js never loads server.js.

Line ~50 still uses model `claude-3-haiku-20240307`. I could not confirm that this model is still served under API version 2026-10-21. The test mocks fetch, so a live 4xx (retired model, or a version/model mismatch) would not be caught. Check Anthropic's models/deprecations page and the 2026-10-21 version notes.

package.json has a `test-api` script (node test-api.js), and there is also deploy.js. Neither was named by the match agent or shown here. If either constructs an Anthropic client, it may use the removed sampling params or old response shapes and break silently under SDK 1.0.

The test relies on the global `fetch`, `Response` and `Headers`, so it assumes Node 18+. SDK 1.0 dropped the node-fetch polyfills, as the removals in package-lock.json show. No `engines` field pins Node, so a deployment on an older Node would fail at runtime. The test is also not wired into an npm script, so CI only runs it if the harness invokes it directly.

The SDK license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0, and new runtime dependencies arrive (@opentelemetry/api, standardwebhooks, json-schema-to-ts, plus @babel/runtime promoted from dev to prod). This is worth noting for license and supply-chain review; it is not a functional problem.

checkFirst: Make one real request to /api/chat with a valid key and confirm claude-3-haiku-20240307 returns 200 under anthropic-version 2026-10-21.
Open test-api.js and deploy.js and grep for `messages.create`, `completions`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` and `content[0]`.
Confirm the deployment's Node version is at least what @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 requires (see its package.json `engines` field).
Decide whether returning an empty 200 when there is no text block is acceptable, or whether server.js should keep erroring in that case.
